Having a claim to a piece of territory makes it harder for others to justify aggression against you. Conversely, if you have a legitimate claim to something, you can honorably use force to obtain it.

You will also find it easier to justify moving against your rivals under the guise of championing someone else's claim.<helptext>

You can expect claimants to approach you for support in pressing their claims to systems or factions held by others. You don't have to take up their cause, but of course it can be to your advantage to champion them and back their quest for a right to which they have an equal or stronger claim.  Indeed, you can approach any of your own nobles yourself if you spot such an opportunity.
    The respect for legitimacy helps keep our society stable.  The use of force on behalf of such claimants will meet no widespread disapproval, provided you honour their claims when the dust settles.  Any advantage you gain in the process will be easy to justify.

The vassal rulers of {factionOf(PlayerCharacter)} and the nobles on {homeSystemOf(PlayerCharacter)} are obliged to respond to your call to arms with their combined military fleets.

The fleet a system can field is directly related to its economic strength, so  increasing the wealth of a system will increase your overall military strength.

Fleets cost a lot to support and a star system cannot send its fleets very far, so the size of the force at your disposal will vary depending on the location you fight over. 

You should consider how much military power an opponent can bring to bear on a location before you commit to combat, and consider the likelihood of allies and enemies on both sides who may choose to join the fight.

Our society is focused on building, maintaining, and supplying the fleets that are necessary to defend ourselves.  If a part of your fleet is damaged in a skirmish, your nobles and rulers will repair and rebuild it over time.
    You should look out for such moments of weakness in those around you.

Don't expect anything other than bad publicity and trouble if you divorce. A divorce dissolves kinship ties, undermining the stability of alliances between houses.  Bad feeling can easily escalate into warfare which stronger factions will be glad to exploit.  Grant divorces to your house members sparingly, and where wrongdoing justifies it.
    Of course, sometimes you may decide a divorce is worth the risk so you can arrange a better marriage elsewhere... despite how others may judge your actions. Think carefully before you act!

An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth

Everyone understands that when a person has dishonorably injured another they are to be punished to the same degree by the aggrieved party. Similarly, acts of goodwill or kindness are to be repaid. You will find it prudent to give your peers as little justification as possible to attack you, and to have them in your debt.<helptext>

Character Tab Enabled: Justice and Social Debt</helptext>

As a leader, you are also responsible for the fate of your subjects.  If you want to be considered a strong but good leader, you should uphold their rights and seek justice on their behalf when they are wronged.  If you do not, opinion of you will drop.

Other leaders will also demand that you mete out justice on their behalf or that of their subjects, and some will even go to war if you do not.

The colony's nobles (and their militaries) are split between loyalists and rebels

Someday you will become an archon - head of a great house, and ruler of a league of factions. The most powerful dynasties in the galaxy do not just rule systems directly, but have many vassal factions pay homage to them.

Your control over the rulers in your faction is not absolute; as long as they do not oppose you they are free to act politically and militarily to their own advantage. To different degrees, each ruler has a right to be the ruler of their system and you will find it hard to justify replacing them.

The potential for powerful and discontent rulers to rebel or change allegiance is high. Work to keep your vassals loyalty, but also keep an eye out for opportunities to seduce a neighbour's vassals.
We can only keep so many vassals honest

Houses are either independent or vassals of other houses, trading protection for economic and military contribution. Rulers are vassals to leaders in a faction, and leaders can be vassals to archons in a league. If you are weak, it is better to submit in vassalage then be conquered or surrender our leadership.

The larger your empire becomes, the harder it will get for our house to manage. If you are independent, you will want to allow some of your rulers to rule their own factions under you as vassal leaders, reducing your direct number of vassals.<helptext>
